newsitem.title: POLAND: ABN-Amro recommends long zloty positions-report.
newsitem.headline: ABN-Amro recommends long zloty positions-report.

text.p: The zloty's future largely depends on a monetary tightening which would improve Poland's current account, but the outlook for the currency is positive, a senior ABN-Amro analyst said in a Thursday report.

Tony Norfield, head of the bank's London Treasury research, said the zloty was less at risk from the widening trade gap than the Czech koruna because Poland's growth has been stronger and high yields were more sustainable.

Earlier this year the Czech Republic had to devalue its currency after foreign investors began winding up their large short-term koruna positions on the fast growth of the current account deficit and slowing economic growth.
"We would recommend long zloty positions, since the high yields give forward points that project a (zloty) depreciation faster than is likely," Norfield said.

"However, it is important that the new government shows its commitment to fiscal tightening so as not to question longer-term financial viability," he said. Poland is scheduled to hold parliamentary elections on September 21.
Norfield predicted the zloty would close the year at around one percent below its parity rate.
The zloty closed at 1.48 percent below parity on Thursday, 3.4560 against the dollar and 1.8820 against the mark.
